questions.q: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 recognises how many categories of disabilities?
questions.e: The RPwD Act 2016 raised the number from 7 under the 1995 Act to 21 specified disabilities.

questions.q: The Salamanca Statement (1994) is an international document on
o: inclusive education and special needs education
questions.e: Adopted at a UNESCO conference in Salamanca, Spain, it called on schools to accommodate all children, including those with special needs.

questions.q: A persistent difficulty in learning arithmetic and number concepts, despite normal intelligence, is called
questions.e: Dyscalculia affects mathematics. Dyslexia affects reading and dysgraphia affects writing.

questions.q: The RTE Act, 2009 guarantees free and compulsory education to children in the age group of
questions.e: Article 21A and the RTE Act 2009 cover children from 6 to 14 years, that is, Classes I to VIII.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. Integration expects the child to adjust to the existing school system.
II. Inclusion means placing children with disabilities in separate special schools.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: In integration the child must fit in. Inclusion changes the school to suit all learners, and does not mean segregation.

questions.q: Under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, private unaided non-minority schools must admit at least what percentage of children in the entry-level class from disadvantaged groups and weaker sections?
questions.e: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act requires at least 25% reservation in entry-level classes of private unaided schools.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a principle of Universal Design for Learning (UDL)?
o: Multiple means of action and expression
A single standard means of assessment for all
questions.e: UDL offers flexibility in how content is presented, how learners show learning, and how they are motivated. A single fixed means for all contradicts it.

questions.q: A student with ADHD often leaves the seat and calls out answers. The most appropriate response for the teacher is to
o: punish the child in front of the class
use structured routines, short tasks, movement breaks and positive reinforcement
seat the child alone at the back permanently
questions.e: Children with ADHD benefit from structure, clear short tasks, planned movement and praise. Punishment and labelling do not address the difficulty.

questions.q: Under the RPwD Act 2016, a 'person with benchmark disability' is one with not less than ______ per cent of a specified disability.
questions.e: The Act defines benchmark disability as at least 40 per cent of a specified disability, unless the disability is defined in measurable terms.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Samagra Shiksha.
I. It subsumes Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and Teacher Education schemes.
II. It covers school education from pre-school to Class XII.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Samagra Shiksha, launched in 2018–19, is an integrated scheme that treats school education as a continuum from pre-school to Class XII.
